# M0-S8: Go and loGo/s packages import each other across workspace modules.
# Each case uses its own fixture so an earlier diagnostic cannot mask a later one.

env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local
mkdir $WORK/bin

# Case 1: a loGo/s package imports a Go package from another workspace module.
cd w1
logos build ./...
logos build -o $WORK/bin/w1$GOEXE ./l/cmd
exec $WORK/bin/w1$GOEXE
stdout '^from-go$'
logos test ./...
stdout '^ok\s+example\.com/l/p'
cd ..

# Case 2: a Go package imports a loGo/s package from another workspace module.
cd w2
logos build ./...
logos build -o $WORK/bin/w2$GOEXE ./g/cmd
exec $WORK/bin/w2$GOEXE
stdout '^from-logos$'
logos test ./...
stdout '^ok\s+example\.com/g/q'
# Plain go ignores .lgo files, so the loGo/s package is not found.
cd g
! go build ./...
stderr 'no required module provides package example\.com/l/p'
cd ../..

# Case 3: a loGo/s package imports only the standard library and runs.
cd std
logos build ./...
logos run .
stdout '^std-ok$'
cd ..

# Case 4: a module holding one Go package and one loGo/s package fails.
cd mixedmod
! logos build ./...
stderr '\[correctness::mixed_module\] module example\.com/m has Go packages \(example\.com/m/a\) and loGo/s packages \(example\.com/m/b\)'
cd ..

# Case 5: a workspace root builds a Go module and a loGo/s module; both binaries run.
cd ws
logos build ./...
logos build -o $WORK/bin/gohello$GOEXE ./gomod
logos build -o $WORK/bin/lgohello$GOEXE ./lgomod
exec $WORK/bin/gohello$GOEXE
stdout '^go-ok$'
exec $WORK/bin/lgohello$GOEXE
stdout '^lgo-ok$'

-- w1/go.work --
go 1.27

use (
	./l
	./g
)

-- w1/l/go.mod --
module example.com/l

go 1.27

-- w1/l/p/p.lgo --
package p

import "example.com/g/q"

func Msg() string { return q.Msg() }

-- w1/l/p/p_test.lgo --
package p

import (
	"testing"

	"example.com/g/q"
)

func TestMsg(t *testing.T) {
	if got := q.Msg(); got != "from-go" {
		t.Fatalf("q.Msg() = %q, want %q", got, "from-go")
	}
	if got := Msg(); got != "from-go" {
		t.Fatalf("Msg() = %q, want %q", got, "from-go")
	}
}

-- w1/l/cmd/main.lgo --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/l/p"
)

func main() { fmt.Println(p.Msg()) }

-- w1/g/go.mod --
module example.com/g

go 1.27

-- w1/g/q/q.go --
package q

func Msg() string { return "from-go" }

-- w2/go.work --
go 1.27

use (
	./l
	./g
)

-- w2/l/go.mod --
module example.com/l

go 1.27

-- w2/l/p/p.lgo --
package p

func Msg() string { return "from-logos" }

-- w2/g/go.mod --
module example.com/g

go 1.27

-- w2/g/q/q.go --
package q

import "example.com/l/p"

func Msg() string { return p.Msg() }

-- w2/g/q/q_test.go --
package q

import (
	"testing"

	"example.com/l/p"
)

func TestMsg(t *testing.T) {
	if got := p.Msg(); got != "from-logos" {
		t.Fatalf("p.Msg() = %q, want %q", got, "from-logos")
	}
	if got := Msg(); got != "from-logos" {
		t.Fatalf("Msg() = %q, want %q", got, "from-logos")
	}
}

-- w2/g/cmd/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/g/q"
)

func main() { fmt.Println(q.Msg()) }

-- std/go.mod --
module example.com/std

go 1.27

-- std/main.lgo --
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
)

func main() {
	_ = context.Background()
	fmt.Println("std-ok")
}

-- mixedmod/go.mod --
module example.com/m

go 1.27

-- mixedmod/a/a.go --
package a

func A() int { return 1 }

-- mixedmod/b/b.lgo --
package b

func B() int { return 2 }

-- ws/go.work --
go 1.27

use (
	./gomod
	./lgomod
)

-- ws/gomod/go.mod --
module example.com/gws

go 1.27

-- ws/gomod/main.go --
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	fmt.Println("go-ok")
}

-- ws/lgomod/go.mod --
module example.com/lws

go 1.27

-- ws/lgomod/main.lgo --
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	fmt.Println("lgo-ok")
}
